hints: Look closely at statement 1. Influenza is caused by a virus, so what will a broad spectrum antibiotic actually do to the harmless bacteria living in that person?

Remember the core rule of resistance: any time bacteria are exposed to an antibiotic, susceptible cells die and any naturally resistant mutants survive to reproduce. Apply this selection pressure idea to all three statements.
walkthrough:
**Recall How Resistance Develops**

Think of it as natural selection in action. Whenever bacteria meet an antibiotic, most die but a few with a resistance mutation survive and multiply.

So the key question is not whether the use is sensible, but whether bacteria are exposed to the antibiotic.

**Check Statement 1 - Antibiotic For Flu**

Influenza is a virus, so antibiotics will not help at all. This is misuse.

However, the broad spectrum antibiotic will still kill many harmless gut and skin bacteria, leaving only resistant ones alive. So 1 can cause resistance.

**Check Statements 2 and 3 - Real Bacterial Targets**

Statement 2 targets Mycobacterium tuberculosis, which is a bacterium. Statement 3 targets bacteria causing sickness in cattle.

In both cases, the antibiotic kills susceptible pathogens but also selects for any resistant mutants in the pathogen and in other exposed bacteria. Both broad spectrum (2) and narrow spectrum (3) use create selection pressure, so both can cause resistance.

**Put It Together**

Since 1, 2 and 3 all expose bacteria to an antibiotic and allow selection for resistant survivors, all three may result in antibiotic-resistant bacteria.

That matches option A.

options.A: Correct and reassuring. All three uses expose bacteria to antibiotics, creating selection pressure where resistant bacteria survive, so 1, 2 and 3 are all included.
options.B: This misses out 3. Even a narrow spectrum antibiotic used correctly in cattle still kills susceptible bacteria and selects for resistant survivors.
options.C: This misses out 2. Using a broad spectrum antibiotic for TB still exposes many bacteria to the drug, so resistant strains can be selected.
options.D: This misses out 1. Giving antibiotics for a viral flu is misuse, but it still kills normal flora and strongly selects for resistant bacteria.
